_comment_family: Bebas Neue with a Cyrillic added to it by a second hand, and a
different file from the Bebas Neue beside it in fonts/ - which is the
first thing to know, because the two are easy to mistake for one face
asked for twice.
The family is what this file's name table says (ID 1), 'Bebas Neue
Cyrillic', and that is what keeps the two apart. bebas-neue.json
declares 'Bebas Neue', so the browser holds two families, each
answering with its own outlines and its own metrics, and fontguard
verifies each by its own name. Had this one been declared as 'Bebas
Neue' too, `registerFace` in js/channels.js would skip it as a family
already present and the channel set in it would quietly be drawn in
the other file.
One cut, so the family alone names it - the same argument
bebas-neue.json makes for itself. Weight 400 is the file's own
usWeightClass, and there is no fvar table, so nothing is interpolated
or synthesised.
Like the original it is a capitals face, and the preset uppercases
every caption under the Snapchat heading anyway (see `uppercase` in
presets/snapchat-caption.json). The Latin accents a French, German or
Portuguese caption needs are all in the file.
It carries no GPOS and no kern table: the pairs are spaced by their
advances alone. At 40px in capitals that is the condensed face doing
what it was drawn to do, not a loss worth reaching for another file
over.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes -
nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the full name, which in this file is
the family itself (name ID 4 carries no 'Regular'). 'Bebas Neue' is
deliberately absent: it is the other face's name, and a machine
answering to it would hand back the other file.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, never a design choice - a block laid out against
the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely different, which is
what fontguard exists to catch before anything is drawn.
Chosen all the same, and written as the opposite of the stack of the
face used beside it. This is the BLOCK face on two channels whose
highlight is an ordinary-width sans - Poppins on conspiracy-central,
Montserrat on noisy-dish - so it falls through the original Bebas
Neue, Anton and Impact - tall condensed capitals - while
Whatever a machine is missing, the block stays the narrow one and the
stack: 'Bebas Neue Cyrillic', 'Bebas Neue', 'Anton', Impact, 'Arial Black', sans-serif
